findings.issue: The 3-second hook does not read as 'gloved hand wiping museum glass'. f6-f72: a puffy, segmented, mannequin-white glove slides in flat from frame right, fingers horizontal, and rotates upright by 3.0 s in a pure black void. No glass surface is perceptible: no dust film, no lit upper edge, no cleared band, no contact reflection - only two out-of-focus grey vertical bars at x~0.05/0.94 that read as cage bars. The 'salt crystals' at 3.0 s are two round white dots (read as dead pixels/stars). The brass glint at the bottom is the only cue of a vitrine.
findings.fix: Make the glass the subject of the first 3 s: (1) dust film on the pane as a visible haze (sRGB ~35-45 under the 3000K top spot, brightest across the top 30% of frame, fine speckle + 2 faint old fingerprints); the wipe mask must leave a ~14%-frame-high band that drops to the near-black velvet, so the clean stripe is unmistakable by 2.0 s. (2) Fingertip contact: only index+middle pads on the glass, hand ~35 deg off the pane, add the pane's front-surface reflection of the fingertip (mirrored, 15% opacity) meeting the real fingertip at the contact point at (0.78,0.52) on 1.23 s. (3) Keep the hand in the wipe pose for 1.2-4.5 s (arc from (0.80,0.50) to ~(0.45,0.42)); rotate to the upright T01 pose only after 4.5 s. (4) Slim the glove (finger width -20%), cotton-weave normal, warm white #E9E4DA at ~0.55 so the knuckle seams disappear. (5) Salt: 6-8 faceted 2-4 px crystals clustered in the cleared band x 0.55-0.70, each twinkling for 3-5 frames as the spot catches them, starting 2.75 s. (6) Dim the two far hood edges to <=8% or drop them in S001.

findings.issue: Dead stretch 4.5-10.5 s: the glove stops, the focus racks off it (f200 = 8.3 s: one fully blurred white glove in black, nothing else), and the navigator's hand only becomes visible ~10-11 s. Six seconds of the opening with no new information right as the vocal enters at 6.6 s.
findings.fix: Have the rack 'find' something: the salt hand starts rising from below frame at 6.6 s at ~25% luminance, is clearly readable (palm, salt sparkles) by 8.5 s and stops one finger short at 11.0 s. Limit the rack so her glove never exceeds ~6 px CoC (both hands should be near-sharp at the 13.25 s end frame as written). Give his hand its cool moon edge and 12 riding salt sparkles from 7.5 s, so the change in focus reveals texture.

findings.issue: The reflection does not read as 'a ship lantern rocking on a deep-blue sea' and the outside does not read as 'a quiet modern museum'. f468/f506: a soft yellow rectangle on a bracket floats over a navy blur with a few white glitter blobs at the right; a hot diagonal orange bar crosses lower centre; at 19.5 s the guard's torch is a hard-edged white triangular wedge stabbing up through the compass at (0.60,0.55) - reads as a render glitch; the restorer's reflection is a grey inverted triangle (V collar) at upper right. Beyond the glass the gallery is pure black.
findings.fix: Sea plate (view_shiplamp as composited): a horizon at ~0.45 of the pane height, lantern-lit swell crests under the lantern whose glints swing with it (6-8 s period, +-6 deg), moon glitter kept to the right third; darken the diagonal orange bar to <=30% or remove it. Torch: replace the wedge with a soft, feathered volumetric beam far in the gallery behind the case, sweeping x 0.85->0.15 over ~0.8 s at <=10% luminance, plus a faint moving pool on the far floor. Outside the glass: two cool moonlit floor shafts and the dark silhouettes of G2/G3 at 8-15% luminance so 'glass = sea, outside = museum' reads. Her reflection: head+shoulder silhouette with a cool rim, not a triangle.

findings.issue: The hidden cut pops. S002 last frame: lantern at ~(0.39,0.29), sea glitter faint, her reflection faint. S003 frame 0: lantern at ~(0.42,0.36) (+0.07 frame height), the glitter at x~0.75 jumps to bright white patches, her reflection brightens and her face appears at the top edge. The hood edges match; the reflected content does not.
findings.fix: Change the S003 side: for its first 12 frames drive the nested sea/lantern view and the mirror pass with S002's end camera and gains (glitter x0.4, reflection opacity = S002 end, lantern at (0.39,0.29)), then ease into the 15 deg arc so the sea slides off by angle. Check f506/f507 as a flip pair - nothing in the pane should move more than 1% of frame.

findings.issue: The three-vitrine track, CH1's spectacle and the S066 preview, renders as black: 82-85% of every frame is below 4% and the mean is ~2%. There is no gallery between the cases (no column, no wall, no teak floor, no moon pools), so the era images read as three dim TV screens in a void, not as reflections in glass. The real vitrine contents are not visible through the glass (only G3b's V mount). The restorer's dim reflection does not show at all. The navigator's head is cut off by the top of G3a's pane. G3c's migrant reads as standing at a counter. The moonlight across the three panes (upper right to lower left) is not visible. After G3c centres at 89.36 the dolly keeps going, so the last 0.7 s (89.4-90.04) is ~70% black, and S025 then cuts back to G3b, which contradicts 'the track stops at G3b'.
findings.fix: Light the room, not just the panes. Raise moonI 1.7->~3.0 and hemi 0.2->~0.45, and lay three arched moon pools on the teak floor in the bottom 22% of frame, one under each case. Put a cast-iron column between each pair of cases with a silver moon edge, and add a cool bounce on the north wall so the brick and columns read at 8-12% (never 0). Target per frame: mean at least 7%, at most 35% of pixels below 4%. Layer each pane: the real contents at 30-40% (G3a needle-route book + sounding lead; G3b empty mount + shards; G3c open case), the era plane above them (raise strength from 0.10-0.42 to 0.25 entering and 0.60 centred), and a diagonal moon glint running from the upper right to the lower left of each pane. Rim-light her with the doorway moon as she walks behind the dolly, so her reflection reads at x ~0.40 as a dark silhouette with a silver edge at ~15-20% of the era brightness. Lower the cabin plate ~0.12 m so the navigator's head sits inside the pane. Use a lower angle in view_pier so the crate and her knees under the case read as seated. Ease out the dolly over the last 0.9 s so G3c centres at 89.36 and holds at x 0.45-0.55 until the cut (90.04). Black must never fill more than 30% of the frame. Keep the cut to S025 (she walks back to G3b), but update S025's transition note to match.

findings.issue: Director note #8 is NOT fixed. The modern gallery night is far darker than every other module. Mean luminance: S023 3-6% (79% of the first frame below 4%), S024 2%, S025 3%, S028 3.5%, S029 1.3% (94% black), against S022 10%, S027 corridor 9%, S036 pier 13%. That is ~25 s of near-black film (83.5-108.9 s) broken only by S026 at 27%. Exposure jumps at cuts: S025->S026 is about +3 stops (3.6% -> 27%) on a 'reflection' transition that should feel like the same pane; S026->S027 is -1.5 stops, and S027->S028 another -1.4 stops.
findings.fix: Set the gallery's base night to the corridor's level: mean 6-10%, at most 40% of pixels below 4%. Raise hemi 0.2-0.3 -> 0.45-0.6 and add moon bounce off the floor pools onto the walls, columns and ceiling, so architecture reads as deep blue (P04 moon silver highlights) instead of 0. For S025->S026, bring S026 down to ~12-15% (exposure 1.3->~0.8, or uEra2 0.32->0.2) and S025 up to ~7%, so the rack from face to hand happens inside one pane at one exposure. Check every first and last frame of S023-S030 against those targets.

findings.issue: The guard's nod must be remembered (S065 reverses it), but it cannot be seen. He stops 12 m away (head ~25 px at 960). The nod is ~0.13 rad (about 7 deg) of neck+head, and it peaks at ~103.52 s, 0.15 s after the 103.37 vocal accent. Frames 2476 and 2481 are indistinguishable. 60% of S028 is pure black. Artefact: for S028's first ~9 frames (101.79-102.17) the torch cone and pool float in empty space before he steps out from behind the column; throughout, the cone is a hard-edged solid white triangle. S029 at ~106.2 s: his 'hand behind the back' IK fails after the +0.28/-1.0 cheat offset, so his left arm sticks out sideways with the palm open, like a dancer.
findings.fix: Move his stop on the same ray (frame x ~0.64) from 12 m to ~7.5 m: about 65% of frame height, head at least 40 px, still between the columns. Nod: 14-16 deg total, 0.35 s down, 0.25 s hold, 0.45 s up, with the bottom of the nod exactly at 103.37. Dip the torch with it, so the floor pool slides ~0.3 m toward her. Give his head and shoulders a moon rim from the doorway side, so the nod reads as a silhouette change. Hide torch and torchCone until his hand clears the column (t >= ~0.4 s). Halve the cone intensity (0.025 -> ~0.012) and feather its edges with dust noise. In S029, re-solve guard.reach('L', ...) after applying the cheat offset, so the left hand stays at the small of his back through the turn (106.9). Let the moon shaft reveal the columns and the ceiling above him, so the top half is not dead black.

findings.issue: Mannequin faces are exposed in the restorer's close-ups (the same problem as note #1). S029: her sharp left profile at ~45% of frame height is lit from brow to chin by the inspection lamp, and the eye reads as a dark socket hole. S025: her profile and her reflection on the empty mount are both lit warm from the front (inspLight 0.14 aimed at her eye plus fillA 0.38), so her reflection is brighter than the wife deep in the glass, which breaks the lock 'her reflection darker than the candle'. The wife's face is a tiny dim shape at (0.62,0.30). The shot's moonlight key and cool edge (lighting spec) are missing.
findings.fix: S029: hood the inspection lamp so it lights only below the nose line (warm on chin and lips, as the keyframe says). Keep the eye and cheek in shadow. Keep a futTop moon edge on the hair, ear and brow, so the look-up at 104.99 reads as the brow lifting into the rim. Step back 0.4 m (head ~35% of frame height) and focus on the lash line. S025: aim inspLight at the mount, not her eye. Turn fillA into a back rim from the SSW doorway (~1 stop under), so her face is at most 50% of the candle plate's luminance, and lower the reflection uMir 0.12->~0.06. Enlarge the home plate (W x1.6) so the wife's never-resolving face oval is 12-15% of frame height at (0.68,0.40), beside the candle bokeh.

findings.issue: The 'through the glass' idea is lost. S026 is bright (27% mean) and reads as a direct shot inside the home, with no glass plane, no gallery reflection, and no exposure link to S025. The restorer's real glove (lower right, ~25% of frame, lit grey) reads as a third hand inside the room touching the bowl, not a fingertip outside the glass. The wife's left hand descends from the top edge as a foreshortened claw ~55% of frame height, gripping the chopsticks from above; the silver bangle is unreadable. Timing: the hand is already in place and still from at least 94.46 to 96.9, so the 'straighten, pause, nudge again' action never plays, and the 95.95 band stop is not marked by the hand freezing.
findings.fix: Put the glass in the shot: dust and a diagonal moon streak on the pane, and a faint cool reflection of the arched doorway across the upper right. Set the home plate ~1.5 stops down (see the S023-S029 grade finding). Crop the real glove to the index fingertip entering at (0.93,0.85), at most 6% of frame, fill 1.0->0.25. Its reflection should be the brighter of the pair, and still faint. Re-pose the hand: wrist low at table height from upper left, fingers horizontal along the chopsticks, thumb and index pinching their ends, bangle clear at (0.52,0.62) per the keyframe. Timing: settle the chopsticks 93.6-94.3, lift and nudge 94.46-95.2, then one last 2 mm nudge that ends exactly at 95.95 (tl 2.70). Hold frozen to 96.85, with the glove reflection freezing too.

findings.issue: The discovery insert does not read as a shirt. The folded shirt is a flat grey slab with drawn lines, and its semicircular collar reads as a briefcase handle, so the whole block reads as a briefcase inside a lined box. The rattan case handle (bottom edge, y 0.94) and the permit with four empty photo corners (x > 0.90) are out of frame, though both are locked rhymes (S031, S040). No grazing light shapes the cotton folds. This is the first half of the T13 cross-era match.
findings.fix: Model the folded shirt properly: a folded collar band with two collar points and a top button, sleeves folded back with visible seams, rounded fold edges (5-8 mm radius), and a cotton weave normal map. The cut hem corner at (0.66,0.68) must read as a missing triangle. Rake the 3500 K inspection lamp at 10-15 deg from frame right (from 108.67) so every fold casts a soft shadow. Frame 5% wider so the handle sits at y 0.94 and the permit edge with two empty corners shows at x > 0.90. pier_waiting S031 must use the same folded shape (fresher colour #6F7F8F) so T13 still matches.

findings.issue: 'She walks into the moonlight; the moon is her key' does not happen. She enters at x ~0.10 in near-black, about 0.7 s before the cut, while the moon pool lies at the right of frame. She is lit by an unmotivated warm hotspot beside G3a's left post (it reads as a lantern by her head; likely the warmFill's specular in the glass). The cases glow flat beige from top to bottom like lightboxes, and the reflected moon is a hard white disc that reads as a bulb inside G3c. The tilted-up opening is 79% black: no timber ceiling or brick. The volumetric beam over the camera's shoulder barely registers. The strip lights on the cases are lilac/pink, which is off-palette.
findings.fix: Start her walk at tl ~1.15 (now 1.75). Lay the main doorway pool across her path at x 0.25-0.45, so at '今' (86.06) she steps into it and reads as a silhouette with a silver rim. Kill or flag the warm hotspot at G3a. Cut the case interior glow 60-70% and let the moon sit softly (bloom, ~70% intensity) inside a faint reflected doorway arch. Add moon bounce on the ceiling and brick so the top third reads as deep blue (5-8%). Raise the shafts 0.07->~0.15 with dust. Make the case strip lights 3000 K warm-white or dark.

findings.issue: At 134.6 ('focus breathes, the faded mark surfaces') the grey-violet stamp mark at (0.60,0.50) is effectively invisible, and the four empty photo corners do not read. That weakens the S037 rhyme. There is no glass cue (dust or reflection) in front of the hand, and the glove ends in a bare wrist with no coat sleeve, so it reads as a disembodied plaster hand.
findings.fix: Breathe the focus 0.5 s around 134.6 so the mark reads as a soft violet ring at ~20% contrast against the paper, with the corners as four small dark triangles. Add faint dust and a moon streak on the glass plane, and bring the dark-grey coat cuff in from the bottom-left edge (keyframe).

findings.issue: The audience cannot tell that this is the future or that the coat is HERS. S070 enters the dissolve already on a high-angle medium of the whole folded coat. The cuff is ~8% of frame height, not the shot list's 30% macro, so the S069->S070 textile dissolve registers position (the worn spot is exactly at (0.42,0.62)) but not scale. The worn spot is a round white dot that reads as a pearl button. The coat reads as a grey shirt (three dark buttons, no lapel, rubbery surface, no aged weave or pilling), and no glass cover edges are visible. Grade: S070 ends as a small plinth in a dark room (mean 21%) and S071 is murky grey-green (25-29%), so neither reads as CT_FUTURE (lowest contrast, slightly high-key, silver-white with a hint of warm). The future looks like the same night museum. S071 at 224.0 also shows a large pale diagonal wedge (the viewer's sleeve) across the top centre that reads as a grey tube.
findings.fix: S070 f0 = 100 mm macro: cuff width ~30% of frame height. Make the worn spot an 18x8 mm elongated, fuzzy-edged pale abrasion (#7A7E80 on the aged #4A4D50) with pilling normal detail centred at (0.42,0.62), not a dot. Pull back along the axis, landing frontal at 222.42, so the lapel and her coat's horn middle button read: the same object she wears in S063. Show the 60x60x50 glass cover with two thin bright edge highlights. Grade both shots CT_FUTURE: walls lifted to pale warm grey (>= 55% luminance), contrast ~0.85, black floor raised, mean >= 35% for the S070 end, S071 and S078. S071: keep the hand registration but soften and pale the sleeve wedge (or crop it above frame) so only the palm and a pale unresolved face blur read.

findings.issue: The plant 'the empty bench at the end, as if waiting for two people' is weak. The far bay window is flat blue panes with no harbour light points, and the bench is not readable as a bench (a warm-lit sill). Her silhouette appears near and large in the left doorway (x ~0.20, ~40% of frame height) instead of small and deep within it at (0.30,0.52).
findings.fix: Add 6-10 warm 1900 K harbour points in the bay window, low, around y 0.50-0.55, and backlight the bench as a clean dark silhouette against them. Put the warm-lit doorway opening at (0.30,0.52) and let her cross it as a small figure (~10-12% of frame height) at 99.5.

findings.issue: The film's 'unforgettable spectacle' reads as a dark, cluttered corridor. Mean luminance is 8-11%, with 60-77% of pixels below 10% grey (f4912, f4962, f5006, f5049) and the moon-pool 'light beat' barely visible. P1 at 205.52 (lamp brightest): the glass shows a bright lantern on a wall bracket against a flat blue wall, with no sea, swell or sail. The museum's own unlit lantern hangs below it (two lanterns, no ocean), and bright white speckle 'confetti' covers the left glass 206.4-207.1. P2 at 207.07 (the CH3 grace, rain finally falling into the bowl): two dotted vertical drip lines and a tiny out-of-focus bowl at the frame's lower-right edge (0.83,0.83) beside an orange door blob. The candle and empty seat do not read and the focus never enters the reflection. P3 at 208.57: the migrant STANDS behind a glowing orange case with the bulb's lampshade cone floating across her chest, so she reads as a vendor at a counter, not seated on her rattan case in a moving crowd. P4 at 210.38: the mother is a large pink, skin-toned blur filling the right 20% (reads as a bare back), with almost no stained-glass colour. End 211.9-213.2: the screen's mullions, dado and glass are not visible, so the 'real present through clear glass, not a reflection' layer is lost and it reads as a cut into night_window. The two lit backs sit at the vanishing point for the whole move, so the destination is shown from frame 0 and is never revealed.
findings.fix: (1) Corridor body to moon-silver: setMoon intensity ~6 -> 12 with sharp-edged arched pools every 4 m (one crossing frame per bar), hemi 0.22 -> 0.4, exposure 1.3 -> 1.7. Target mean 16-20% with <= 40% of pixels below 10%; walls and coffers should read in deep blue P02/P03, never black. (2) Each era image fills its vitrine glass (size x1.4), +0.7 stop on the per-pane grade expo, blur -> 0.002 at peak, so each pane is a lit, coloured world against the silver corridor. P1: reframe view_shiplamp wider (lamp at the pane's upper third, >= 60% of the pane moonlit swell with glitter, sail corner at the edge), and dim the museum lantern prop or place it below the reflected horizon. P2: zoom view_home_rain so the eave bowl sits at the pane centre (0.5,0.55) at ~25% of pane height. Make the rain 3-5 cm motion-blurred streaks back-lit by the door lamp (not dots), and rack focus into the reflection 206.9-207.6. Kill the speckle glitter on P1's glass at grazing angle. P3: re-stage view_pier so she sits on the case (case at knee height), bulb shade out of frame top, crowd crossing behind. P4: re-light view_chapel so the mother is a dove-grey back with stained-glass colour pools on her shoulders at ~40% pane height (no skin-tone mass). (3) Present (E): portal gain 0.3 until tl 5.0 (a small warm point), then up to 1.0 by 7.6, and keep the screen's timber mullions and dado plus a 10-15% corridor reflection on its glass visible in the last 1.5 s, so the two backs are seen THROUGH real glass at rest.

findings.issue: The turning point of her arc is hard to read. The diamond quarry reflection is a small pink lump with a dark slash at 191.88 (f4605) and a blank white heart-shaped blob at 192.2 (f4613). It does not read as her face, the 'unease' cannot be seen, and the lift of her eyes on '还' is invisible. From ~193.0 her gloved hands rise to chest height in the centre-left (x 0.30-0.60, y 0.40-0.85), directly over the guard's back, blocking the very sightline the shot is about for the rest of the shot. The gloves are blocky, segmented white shells and the open-palm raise reads as waving or surrender. At 193.9 a stray finger/glove shell sits at (0.47,0.85). The right glove only starts ~193.4 (shot list 192.7). The end fist with the folded gloves is held up in front of his back at (0.33,0.55) rather than low-left (0.36,0.70).
findings.fix: Keep her hands in the lower-left foreground, under his silhouette. Hand targets in x 0.15-0.45, y 0.65-0.95, never above y 0.60 and never overlapping his back (x 0.18-0.40, y 0.45-0.75); if needed, lower the camera ~8 cm so his back rides higher. Glove removal on the shot list's clock: right glove 192.7-193.6 as a fingertip pinch, cuff stretch and slide-off; left 193.9-194.4; folded 194.6; grip and turn 194.97. Diamond: carry 'the lift of her eyes' as motion, a 6-8 deg upward head tilt of the reflection at 191.88. Render the reflected face as a moonlit silhouette (profile edge rimmed by the moon from behind-right, face plane >= 1.5 stops under the panel colour) and enlarge the quarry's mirror view ~x1.3 so the head shape reads at 960 px.

findings.issue: The eye CU is a bald, pink, three-quarter mannequin head with sculpted closed lids, a huge ear and a grey cap: the mask is fully exposed and there is no eye, so the emotional beat ('迷茫的眼睛') and the T05 match (needle pivot (0.46,0.50) -> pupil) both fail; the eye region sits at ~(0.53,0.30). No beard/scar/head-cloth; the wind-in-strands action is off (strands.visible=false). Director note #1 not fixed for S010.
findings.fix: Restage as a low-key eye-line CU: camera behind his right shoulder at ~3/4 back, 100 mm, the stern window lattice (frame left) as a dusk-blue backlight so his profile is near-silhouette; only brow ridge, lid line and eye-socket rim take the cool light, lantern warm only on the cheek edge/ear. Put a 3-4 px wet catch-light exactly at (0.46,0.50) - that is the 'pupil' for the T05 match - and play the 51.39 blink as the catch-light vanishing for 4 frames. Indigo head-cloth over a topknot (not a cap), loose strands visible and moving. Skin desaturated weathered brown, not pink.

findings.issue: Frame 0 (and 41.78 s): a frontal, evenly warm-lit mannequin face fills the centre, eyes down; the costume reads as a modern French sailor - blue beret and crew-neck sweater - not an indigo head-cloth over a topknot and a cross-collar jacket. Same costume in S010.
findings.fix: Head-cloth: wrapped indigo cloth with the topknot bump at the crown/back; jacket: faded indigo cross-collar (交领). Light: lantern from behind-left as a 3/4 back key so the face is 60-70% in shadow (nose ridge, brow, cheekbone warm), dusk-blue hatch light as a top rim on the head-cloth and shoulders. Open as an MS (40 mm, head ~30% of frame height), camera ~15 deg below eye-line, so the upward look reads as a shape, not a mask.

findings.issue: Note #3 only partially fixed: f1010-f1022 (42.1-42.6 s) is still a near-black frame (a dark beam with a sliver of blue), i.e. u=0.5 is unreadable. Then the sail already fills the frame by 43.2 s and sits static until the cut, so the reveal arrives 0.7 s before '帆' (43.94) and the 'still rising' hand-off to S008 is not felt. The sky is starry saturated royal blue, while S008 is dusk navy with afterglow.
findings.fix: Aim the path at the hatch from 1.6 s so the dusk-blue opening stays in frame and grows from ~15% to 100% of frame by 43.0 s; lantern bounce on the coaming underside so no frame of the passage falls below ~25/255 mean. Re-time so the sail fills on 43.94 and keeps rising after (battens sliding down >=5% of frame/s to the cut). Grade the sky to S008's dusk (#0E1B30->#2E4A6E, no star field).

findings.issue: The patch lock fails: it renders pale neutral grey-white (~#A8ACA8) with white stitching on the OUTSIDE of a wide cuff band - reads as a laundry label, not the wife's pale-blue cloth (#7D9CBB, = her blouse which reads clearly blue in S017). The fold-back gesture is absent (the three frames are identical). The fingertip 'cracks' are black squiggles that read as insects.
findings.fix: Patch #7D9CBB hand-woven texture, pilled/shiny centre, double knot at the upper-right corner. Play the gesture: 52.75-53.0 s the left thumb+index lift the cuff edge 2-3 cm and turn it back to reveal the patch inside, then the index/middle pads settle on it (contact (0.50,0.52), fingers 30 deg from upper right) and hold. Cracks as 1 px low-contrast hairlines; skin desaturated and darker.

findings.issue: On '刻' (36.99 s) the thumb enters from the upper left far out of focus as a smooth pink blob that covers ~40% of the frame at f895 - it reads as a foreign object, not a seaman's thumb wiping salt off the 午 rim.
findings.fix: Bring the thumb in along the rim at the lower left (the 午 mark, where the salt bloom is), in the focal plane, thumb width <=15% of frame height, weathered brown skin (~#8C5E40), a salt crust on the knuckle; it wipes ~2 cm along the rim, leaving brighter brass. The travelling lantern glint stays as is - it works.

findings.issue: The match itself works (T03 registry holds), but the left brass weight reads as an emissive orange tube (a light-box), and the stern-window light is four horizontal blue stripes across the right 40% of the chart - it reads as blinds and pre-empts S021's louvres. The '蓝' corner lift (32.77 s) is barely visible.
findings.fix: Weight as solid dull brass (#8E7348) with one highlight, no emission. The 直棂 stern window as one soft vertical dusk-blue band at x ~0.78-0.95 with thin vertical bar shadows, keeping the islet (0.62,0.40) in the lamp pool. Make the corner lift 4-6 cm and readable at 48 fps.

findings.issue: The needle barely moves: the first and last frames differ by <=2 deg, so '摆动两三次…在“认得南”时稳稳停住' has no visible settle on 49.77.
findings.fix: Start 8 deg clockwise of south, 2.5 damped cycles, dead still from 49.77 at the T05 pivot (0.46,0.50).

findings.issue: The cumulus bases sit right on the horizon line as hard-edged grey-brown lumps; they read as rock islands floating on the sea.
findings.fix: Lift the cloud bases to y ~0.28-0.32 (horizon at 0.42), feather their undersides, add a thin stratus band with the last warm underlight; keep the coast light at the left and the junk as is.

findings.issue: In S022's opening frames the shore light (0.30,0.58) has a square box-shaped halo (~30 px), clearly a sprite edge, while focus is on it. sea_deck also still replaces the engine grain with its own module grain (note #7).
findings.fix: Use a radial falloff sprite (or bloom only) for the shore light. Remove the module grain quad and return grain: 0.04 to the engine.

findings.issue: CH2 lock 'first touch the patch, then look at the shore light' does not read. 145.1-146.7 his left hand hovers over his upturned right palm, fingertips 1-2 cm off a pale-blue rectangle stuck on the OUTSIDE of the cuff; nothing turns the cuff back, nothing touches the patch. Hands at mean 13/255 (note #4 only partly fixed). At 146.7 ('某个', the eye lift) the frame is still on the hands; the tilt then whips through the dark coat in ~0.8 s. The end frame (147.5-148.67) is a fully lit bald mannequin profile - bare skull under a small cap, a large crisp ear, a catch-light dot for an eye (note #1). Hands read as lumpy rubber (salt crust as warts).
findings.fix: 145.14 left index+middle fingertips hook the right cuff edge and fold it back 3-4 cm, revealing the patch on the INSIDE (bible lock); pads rest on it with real contact 145.4-146.0, thumb rubs once. Lift the hands 1-1.3 stops (moon key on hands, stern-lantern 1950K kicker from frame right) to mean ~30/255 with the patch the brightest mid-tone; salt as fine glints (2-3 px) not bumps. Start the tilt at 145.9, arrive on the eye at 146.7, hold to the cut. Final framing MCU 75-85 mm, face mostly silhouette against the deep-blue sea: moon rim from upper right on brow/nose/cheek edge only, head-cloth pulled down over the skull and ear (ear in shadow), catch-light in the near eye; shore light at (0.40,0.46) kept for the S046 light-match, bokeh ~4% of frame height so it is the brightest thing in frame.

findings.issue: Director note #6 is NOT fixed. The companion lies flat on his back, legs straight and arms crossed on his chest, like a corpse, not 'curled against a rope coil, shivering'. The coat is a rigid board. At 213.6 it is a cream/tan flat panel held at the navigator's chest (wrong colour: PROP_OUTERCOAT is brown #5B4634). At 214.25 it flies across ~1.5 m as a stiff sheet while his hands stay at the lantern, with no contact. At 215.3 it stands on the boy's chest as an upright dark slab. The navigator never bends or reaches. The left-fingers-on-right-cuff patch beat (215.3) is ambiguous: both hands are clasped at his waist.
findings.fix: Have the navigator take one step and kneel on his right knee beside the boy (213.2-213.6, figure to ~(0.42,0.55)). His hands keep the coat by the collar all the way until it touches the boy's shoulder at 214.25, then release. Use a cloth drape (blend 3 baked poses: bunched -> half-open in the wind -> laid over shoulder-to-hip with folds running left to right), outer brown #5B4634 facing the lens with the lining only as a sliver. Boy: curled on his left side facing the lens, knees drawn up, head on the rope coil at right, hands tucked under his chin, face hidden by the collar; collar tug at 214.9 as a 5 cm hand rise. 215.3: navigator (still kneeling or rising) with left fingertips clearly inside his turned-back right cuff at (0.36,0.62), rim-lit by the lantern, held 1 beat.
